title: Bridgeweek Communal Priority Dossier (v0.1)
summary: Working dossier to drive a one-week cross-functional alignment sprint (Bridgeweek) to rebaseline company priorities, finalize Q2 OKR candidates, and surface critical dependencies for execution.
audience: Executive leadership, product leads, engineering managers, go-to-market leads
purpose: Create a compact set of prioritized company-level initiatives and an operational playbook for the Bridgeweek event. Capture decisions, owners, risks, and immediate follow-ups so the all-hands can land clear commitments.
narrative: Why this exists: momentum and usage signals from the last quarter show uneven progress across candidate priorities (Optimize, Dedicated, Private). We need a short, high-bandwidth week to: 1) choose which initiatives get company-level focus for the next 90 days, 2) lock owners and measurable adoption targets, and 3) identify tactical lift to de-risk launch dependencies. This dossier is intentionally light-weight — it mixes structured OKR candidates with operational scenarios and a short contingency tree for capacity or model regressions.
agenda: Day 0: Pre-reads distributed (24 hrs before) — short one-pager per initiative + key metrics snapshot
Day 1 AM: Kickoff — 45m leadership framing, 30m quick Q&A; PM syncs to split into focus groups
Day 1 PM: Focus groups (product + eng + go-to-market) — align scope and success metrics (90m)
Day 2: Engineering feasibility and SRE capacity sync (2h) — surface blockers and ETA adjustments
Day 3: Customer & Sales readiness review (1.5h) — refine launch asks and enablement
Day 4: Decision forum (2h) — leadership chooses top 3 company priorities and approves owners
Day 5: All-hands prep & comms — finalize slide slate, one-pager, and action tracker
proposed_okrs: Objective A: Reduce per-token inference cost for top 3 hosted models while preserving P95 latency. KR1: 20% reduction in average per-token cost for hosted API traffic by end of quarter. KR2: Maintain P95 latency within 1.2x of baseline during peak traffic. KR3: Enable cross-region caching for two EU regions.

Objective B: Ship Redwood Dedicated beta with predictable autoscaling policies. KR1: Deliver Dedicated onboarding flow (self-serve) with telemetry in Console. KR2: Validate autoscale policy under 3 simulated workload patterns and document fallback behaviors. KR3: Sign 2 pilot customers onto Dedicated reserved pools.

Objective C: Harden Private deployment security posture for regulated customers. KR1: Complete KMS/HSM integration playbook and publish compliance checklist. KR2: Complete 3rd-party pen-test remediation items. KR3: Deliver on-prem install churn < 2 major escalations for first 5 customers.

Cross-cutting: Increase model-serving reliability and observability. KR1: Reduce token-drop errors by 60%. KR2: Implement traceable sample-by-sample QA for 80% of canaries. KR3: Create cost/quality dashboard and run monthly regression alerts.
candidate_priorities_notes: Optimize pipeline (batching, KV caching, quantization): high ROI but cross-team work and requires infra sprints.
Dedicated capacity: sales-facing, highest near-term revenue motion, needs onboarding UX and billing contract template.
Private (VPC/on-prem): strategic for regulated customers; longer sales cycles, heavy security/compliance work.
Developer experience: incremental wins (SDKs, docs) yield high activation; can be run as continuous improvement alongside big bets.
decision_criteria: Effort: engineering cost and infra footprints (GPU hours), delivery risk
Strategic leverage: unlocks other initiatives or closes enterprise deals
Customer urgency: documented asks from >=3 pilots or enterprise prospects
scenarios_and_contingencies: Scenario 1: If Dedicated pilot uptake is lower than forecast (<=1 pilot), reallocate 30% capacity budget to Optimize pipeline work and increase public benchmarks to drive demand.

Scenario 2: If a major model regression is detected during canary (quality drop > 15% on sentinel prompts), trigger automatic fallback to previous model variant and pause any rollout; run forensic eval and owner review within 48 hours.
Scenario 3: If on-prem installers encounter HSM integration blockers, delay Private onboarding by one sprint and offer a hosted bridge solution with contractual SLAs to affected customers.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Overcommitting engineering across multiple priorities. Mitigation: cap company-level priorities to top 3, require team-level reprioritization plans.
Risk: Ambiguous success metrics lead to misaligned delivery. Mitigation: require KRs to have exact measurement sources (Console metric, GA event, billing delta).
Risk: Sales/customer expectations mismanaged during Bridgeweek. Mitigation: Sales-run comms template and committed SLA for updates within 72 hours after decisions.
open_questions: Which two models do we classify as 'top 3 hosted models' for Objective A — inference cost: foundation repo vs customer favorites?
Do we have capacity to run the three workload simulations for Dedicated without impacting production SLAs?
Who signs off on the 'hosted bridge' contractual offering for Private customers (legal + product + sales)?
